meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-02 | Start: 15:00 PT | Duration: 49 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Ethan Cole (Sentinel CTO), Maya Ruiz (Platform Eng Manager), Leo Zhang (ML Infra), Ava Thompson (Finance), Jared Kim (Security)
summary: Quarterly-style health and economics readout: review of November usage and cost trends, discussion of two reliability incidents and mitigation steps, sizing options for Dedicated capacity vs continued Hosted with burst, and agreement on next steps for a technical deep dive and cost forecast.
topics: Two reliability incidents (KV cache eviction + degraded retry logic)
Dedicated sizing vs Hosted with burst
Roadmap items: caching, batching, rollout cadence
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we've got about 50 minutes, i wanted to run through November numbers and the incidents you hit last week and then chat about options for next quarter. hey Ethan, can you kick us off with a quick context on what changed in November?
[00:20] Ethan: Yeah, sure. hey all. so November we saw a big uptick in user-initiated summary requests after product launch, about 3x baseline in the first two weeks. that pushed token volume up and then we hit two separate blips, one early morning KV cache eviction and then later some degraded retries in our client layer.
[00:40] Maya: to add, most of the traffic spike was from our mobile web flow, the token distribution skewed short->medium responses, but bursty. we did see sustained concurrency peaks around 11am and 4pm PT.
[01:05] Jordan: got it. Priya, you have the cost and perf slide?
[01:10] Priya: yeah i pulled the raw numbers. overall Redwood invoice went up 62% month-over-month, but unit cost per token rose only a bit. the big driver was just volume and high tail concurrency causing less efficient batching. also we found a couple of long-running streams that didn't hit KV cache reuse patterns so they were more expensive.
[01:35] Ava: quick question on the 62% — is that purely hosted invoices or does it include any caching credit you ran?
[01:40] Samir: that's all hosted usage line items; we haven't applied any dedicated credits here. if you move to Dedicated you'd see a different curve where throughput is predictable and unit economics change.
[02:00] Ethan: can you show the projection if we kept hosted but tune batching and caching? how much wiggle room is there without committing to Dedicated?
[02:15] Priya: i prepared two scenarios: tuned-hosted and dedicated-reserved. tuned-hosted assumes we enable more aggressive kv prefix caching, bump batch windows in low-latency tolerant routes, and enable our suggested quantization for your model family; that saves roughly 18-25% on token spend depending on tail behavior. Dedicated-reserved gives predictable throughput — you get about 35-45% lower unit cost at committed throughput but you trade flexibility.
[02:50] Jared: from security we need to confirm audit log retention and KMS options for Dedicated. can you confirm encryption in transit and at rest and HSM support?
[03:05] Jordan: yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated integrate with customer KMS and HSM via our keywrap flow, audit logs are available and can be pushed to your SIEM. i'll attach the SOC2 plus Private deployment security addendum.
[03:30] Leo: on the incidents — what caused the KV eviction? logs showed eviction triggered at ~03:12 PT and several requests fell back to cold KV lookups which spiked latency.
[03:50] Priya: great question. in that window your prefix reuse dropped because of a rollout you did to the mobile summarizer—there was slightly different prompt formatting so cache keys didn't match. the runtime's eviction policy then reclaimed a smaller working set under memory pressure; that combined created the cascade.
[04:20] Maya: so it's basically a cache key mismatch more than memory shortage?
[04:25] Priya: a bit of both. prompt normalization would have prevented many misses, but memory pressure accelerated eviction. we recommended a small config change to increase the working set for your busiest pool which should reduce miss rate during peaks.
[04:50] Ethan: what about the degraded retry logic? that seemed like a client-side problem but we saw retries backlog the system.
[05:05] Jordan: we observed your client retries were aggressive (3x immediate retry) and that amplified tail latency; Priya's team suggested exponential backoff and 10s client-side jitter to avoid reheating the hot path.
[05:25] Priya: additionally we can implement server-side early shedding for non-critical routes so critical requests get through during congestion.
[05:40] Ava: finance wants a short-term forecast so we can decide on committed capacity before end of year. can you give a 90-day cost with tuned-hosted vs Dedicated?
[05:55] Priya: yes — Jordan will share the spreadsheet but summary: tuned-hosted is forecasted to increase spend 20-30% vs current month if volumes keep growth; Dedicated (small pool) would be roughly flat to down 5% but requires a commit.
[06:20] Jared: any compliance caveats with Dedicated? is there any change to log handling or access control?
[06:30] Jordan: Dedicated gives you tenant isolation and dedicated GPUs; audit logs and RBAC remain, we can integrate with your SSO SAML and push logs to your CloudWatch or Splunk. there is a slightly different operational model for patching windows but we offer SLA windows to coordinate.
[06:55] Leo: for the technical deep dive — can Priya show exactly how the KV cache lifetime is computed and how prefix matching works? we need to validate it against our prompt variants.
[07:10] Priya: absolutely. i'll bring a 90-minute session and we'll walk through normalization, key hashing, and eviction thresholds. we'll also run a quick replay of your November traces to show miss patterns.
[07:35] Ethan: excellent. one more on quantization — you mentioned savings but any quality delta we should be worried about?
[07:45] Priya: with 8-bit quant and calibration for your model, we expect negligible quality regressions for summarization tasks; we'll run side-by-side evals with your test prompts. if you need ultra-high fidelity we can land on mixed-precision routes per route.
[08:10] Maya: ok, on roadmap items — you talked about batching config auto-tuning. can that be enabled per route?
[08:20] Priya: yes, we can set per-route batching windows and priority classes. we'll recommend defaults then iterate based on token distribution. that usually captures most of the low-hanging unit cost gains.
[08:40] Samir: i want to call out a smaller operational ask — better tracing across retries. right now it's hard to tie a retry to an original user session in your logs. we can add a correlation id header through the SDK.
[08:57] Leo: perfect, we need that for debugging.
[09:05] Ethan: are there any quick wins we can take immediate?
[09:10] Priya: yes: (1) prompt normalization to reduce KV key churn, (2) soften client retry backoff, (3) enable per-route caching on summarizer, (4) short-term bump to working set for critical pool. those 4 typically cut tail inefficiencies quickly.
[09:35] Ava: finance — when Jordan sends the forecast, please include a sensitivity for +25%/+50% volume so we can plan.
[09:45] Jordan: will do.
[09:50] [15:10] Jordan: shifting to SLA and availability — you had two incidents, do you want Redwood to run a post-incident review with your SREs?
[10:05] Ethan: yes, a joint post-mortem would be helpful. prioritize timeline, impact, and remediation.
[10:15] Priya: we'll prepare a short incident timeline and three recommended mitigations; Samir will coordinate the PM follow-through.
[10:30] Jared: security detail — if we move to Dedicated, how long before we can rotate keys and have the build pipeline validated? we need to keep rotating keys monthly.
[10:45] Jordan: key rotation is supported; it requires a short handoff window but we can make it seamless. i'll add the KMS rotation doc to the next email.
[11:00] Maya: on rollout cadence — we want canary percent control per region, and ability to rollback model variants quickly. how flexible is Redwood's rollout tooling?
[11:15] Priya: our Console supports canaries by traffic weight, per-region routing, and automatic fallback policies. you can pin a route to a model variant or set automatic rollback on latency or error regression. we'll demo that in a future session.
[11:40] Ethan: curious if Redwood has a recommended guardrail for token limits per user session — we need to cap runaway requests.
[11:50] Samir: yes we support per-token and per-request limits; we can create quotas and soft-fail with meaningful error codes so client can backoff.
[12:05] Ava: any differences in billing for error retries? do retries count additional tokens billed?
[12:15] Jordan: billing is per successful token output; retries that re-execute segments are billed for tokens generated. that's why avoiding retries and leveraging server-side shedding matters.
[12:35] Ethan: ok let's confirm the timeline: Jordan sends forecast + Dedicated options by 12/06; Maya uploads logs by 12/04; Priya schedules the deep dive week of 12/14. Samir will run the post-mortem doc.
[12:55] Priya: noted. i'll also prepare a small script to replay your traces against tuned-hosted config to demonstrate savings.
[13:10] Jordan: anything else on adoption or roadmap items?
[13:15] Maya: one ask — we'd like clearer cost attribution per product feature. can Redwood provide token-level tagging so we can map spend to feature owner?
[13:30] Priya: yes, we support route and token tagging; we'll show how to emit tags and then export per-tag cost in the Console.
[13:45] Leo: last technical note — please confirm how your runtime chooses kernels for quantized models; we need to ensure compatibility with our GPU fleet if Dedicated.
[13:58] Priya: runtime performs architecture and sequence-length-aware kernel selection; for quantized paths we select quant-friendly kernels and fall back to fp16 for unsupported ops. we'll detail the GPU compatibility matrix in the deep dive.
[14:20] Ethan: thanks, this was useful. Jordan, Priya, Samir — any closing notes?
[14:28] Jordan: i'll send the forecast + SLA + security addendum. Priya will schedule the deep dive. Samir will assemble the post-mortem skeleton.
[14:40] Samir: i'll also follow up with a one-pager for Finance summarizing the cost options.
[14:50] AvA: thanks everyone.
[14:55] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and schedule next steps. bye.
questions: What specific config change will reduce KV misses?
How much can tuned-hosted realistically save vs Dedicated?
Can Redwood integrate with our KMS and support monthly key rotation?
